1965 Shelby Cobra Backdraft Replica Packs a Nasty, Built 427ci V8 and a Five-Speed Manual From Tremc
10 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
Sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this 427 Shelby Cobra will give you "the biggest adrenaline rush you can get with a plate." That’s probably not very far from the truth, if you’re into small and nimble two-seat roadsters with big American motors under the hood.
The AC Cobra, mostly known and sold in the United States as the Shelby Cobra, was a sports car produced between 1962 and 1967 by British company AC Cars and featuring a Ford V8 engine under the hood. It quickly gained a cult following, and since the 1980s various replicas have been produced by a huge number of companies, aiming to continue the spirit of the original.
This 1965 Shelby Cobra is a Backdraft Replica that “combines the timeless styling of an iconic American roadster with modern performance and a thoroughly built 427ci V8.” Despite its stated year, it’s quite thoroughly ready for the late 2020s, finished in Sterling Gray with white racing stripes, and featuring the classic proportions of the original along with muscular fender flares, side-exit exhaust pipes, and a stance that easily “captures the spirit of the original Shelby Cobra.”
It has a mere 3,586 miles since it was built, so “this example offers an exciting opportunity to own a high-performance roadster with unmistakable vintage-inspired styling.” Under the hood resides a 427ci V8 featuring Edelbrock aluminum cylinder heads, an Eagle forged crankshaft, and Mahle forged pistons.
The performance components are a strong foundation, but the V8 is also paired with an engaging Tremec five-speed manual transmission, “giving the driver direct control over the power delivery.” The Backdraft Racing platform mixes classic Cobra allure with modern technology, “resulting in a replica that delivers the visual impact of the original while offering a contemporary approach to performance.”
Inside, the black interior emphasizes the roadster's driver-focused ethos, with an open-top configuration mixed with “a straightforward cockpit designed around the essentials of performance driving.” The conclusion is simple: “With its extensively equipped 427ci V8 , Tremec five-speed manual transmission, distinctive Sterling Gray finish, and only 3,586 miles since completion, this 1965 Shelby Cobra Backdraft Replica offers an exciting blend of vintage racing inspiration and modern performance,” according to the dealership.
Of course, this replica isn’t coming to a new garage on the cheap: the company wants no less than $114,900 to part ways with it. But then again, Shelby Cobras have always been an expensive hobby, and no one would expect them to sell on the cheap, instead suspecting foul play rather than an honest surprise. What do you think? Would you make this your latest addition to a growing collection or the start of one?
